newsitem.title: CHINA: China interbank market rates (CHIBOR) mixed.
newsitem.headline: China interbank market rates (CHIBOR) mixed.

text.p: Following is the China Interbank Offered Rate (CHIBOR) for Tuesday issued by the official Xinhua news agency on behalf of the People's Bank of China, the central bank.
The figures represent weighted averages and not closing prices and are annual percentage rates.
Turnover fell to 680 million yuan from a thin 828 million yuan with the seven-day contract the most actively traded.
Traders said activity was dull on both the first-tier and second-tier of the interbank market.

First-tier members - including short-term financial centres, money brokerages run by the central bank, and state banks - borrowed little short-term funds on the interbank money market, preferring to borrow on the intebank state debt market, where interest rates were lower, traders said.
"Only a few financial centres, including those from Shanghai and Beijing, traded a few contracts," one trader said.

On the second tier part of the market, where non-banking financial institutions trade through the financial centres, sentiment was hurt by the recent poor performance of domestic A share markets, traders said.

"Securities brokerages, who are major borrowers on the market, have traded little in the past few days," said a second trader. "Consoliation on the A share markets in the past few days has made them need less money."

Brokerages typically borrow money on the interbank market to help balance their accounts. Traders said they expected the interbank rates to stay around current levels in slow trading over the next few days.
